clues.text: This city sits in the north of Tasmania, in Australia. Two Esk rivers meet here and join to form the River Tamar.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside northern Tasmania where the two Esk rivers join

source.quote: Launceston ( LON-sess-tən) is a city in the north of Tasmania, Australia, at the confluence of the North Esk and South Esk rivers where they become the River Tamar (kanamaluka).

clues.text: This city has a sea-side climate with four clear seasons. In summer it is much warmer than the south of the island.
clues.narrowing: rules out places without four distinct seasons and a summer warmer than the island's south

source.quote: The city has a maritime climate with four distinct seasons and is appreciably warmer than the south of the island during summer.

clues.text: Europeans settled here in March 1806. It is one of the oldest cities in Australia, and many old buildings still stand.
clues.narrowing: rules out Australian cities settled later than 1806 or without many historic buildings

source.quote: Settled by Europeans in March 1806, Launceston is one of Australia's oldest cities and it has many historic buildings.

clues.text: This city was the first in Australia to be lit by hydro power. No city in the land had such lights before it.
clues.narrowing: rules out all but the first Australian city lit by hydroelectricity

source.quote: Launceston also had the first use of anaesthetic in the Southern Hemisphere, it was the first Australian city to have underground sewers, and it was the first Australian city to be lit by hydroelectricity.

clues.text: Only Hobart has more folks in Tasmania. This city comes next as the isle's clear second city.
clues.narrowing: confirms the second most populous city in Tasmania after Hobart

source.quote: Launceston is the second most populous city in Tasmania after the state capital, Hobart.
